title_ar: ترحيب بضيف موريتانيا السيد المصطفى بن الإمام الشافعي
title_en: A Welcome to Mauritania’s Guest, al-Sayyid al-Mustafa ibn al-Imam al-Shafiʻi
body_ar: وطني يرحب بالكريم النافع المصطفى نجل الإمام الشافعي بالمصقع البطل الهمام المرتضى ذي العز و الذكر الرفيع الذائع خدن المروءة و المكارم و العلى و الجود و الخلق الجميل الرائع من ينصر المظلوم دون تردد و يفك أسر المستغيث الخانع لا فرق في أفضاله و نواله بين اللجوج و ذي العفاف القانع كل ينال نصيبه من سيبه ببشاشة و تحبب و تواضع ورث المكارم عن أبين أعزة شاعت علاهم في الفضاء الشاسع إن الأكارم من سلالة جاكر حاطوا المفاخر بالبناء الواسع فيدل واقعهم على ماضيهمُ و يدل ماضيهم على ذا الواقع هم مشترو كل المكارم و العلى يغلون في أثمانها للبائع فالعلم فيهم و الشجاعة و الهدى و الجود معْ شرف النفوس الشائع إرث يورثه على طول المدى و صعابه متبوعهم للتابع جاكان أركان العلوم و قبلة ال مظلوم مأمنه و عز الخاضع أعراضهم معصومة محفوظة و عروضهم مقسومة كودائع في كل عصر يظهرون لشعبنا علما يشار له كنجم ساطع فالله ينصرهم و يبقي ذكركم و يديم نعمتهم بخير تتابع
body_en:
[Verse. Rendered as prose, line by line; the Arabic is the operative text.]

*My country bids welcome to the noble and beneficent one, al-Mustafa, son of the Imam al-Shafi'i,*

*to the eloquent one, the valiant and resolute champion, the well-pleasing, possessed of honour and of high and far-spread renown,*

*the close companion of manliness, of noble deeds and high aspiration, of open-handedness and of fine and splendid character;*

*one who comes to the aid of the wronged without hesitation, and looses the bonds of the abject soul who calls for help.*

*In his favours and his gifts he makes no distinction between the importunate and the chaste and contented man:*

*each receives his share of his bounty, with a cheerful face, with affection and with humility.*

*He inherited these noble qualities from forefathers of honour, whose eminence spread through the widest reaches.*

*The noble ones of the line of Jakar have hedged their titles to glory about with a broad edifice;*

*their present state points back to their past, and their past points forward to this present state.*

*They are the buyers of every noble quality and every height, and they bid the price up high for the seller.*

*Knowledge is in them, and courage, and right guidance, and generosity, together with a widely known nobility of soul —*

*an inheritance passed down through the length of time, its hardships and all, from the one followed to the one who follows.*

*Jakan are the pillars of the sciences, the qiblah of the wronged, his place of safety and the honour of the lowly.*

*Their honour is inviolable and guarded, and their goods are apportioned out like things held in trust.*

*In every age they raise up for our people a banner of knowledge, pointed to like a shining star.*

*So may God grant them victory, and keep your memory alive, and make their favour endure in unbroken good.*

flags.context: إن الأكارم من سلالة جاكر ... جاكان أركان العلوم
options: Jakar / Jakan, a Mauritanian lineage name, in two forms
a single name inconsistently spelled in the source
a place name rather than a lineage
flags.note: The poem names the addressee’s line twice in two different forms, سلالة جاكر and جاكان. Both are transliterated as they stand rather than normalised to one spelling. A Mauritanian reader will recognise the family; the transliteration should be confirmed by the Sheikh’s office before publication.

flags.arabic: ضيف موريتانيا السيد المصطفى بن الإمام الشافعي
options: al-Sayyid al-Mustafa ibn al-Imam al-Shafiʻi, a visiting dignitary
the guest is being welcomed on behalf of the country, i.e. a state visit
al-Mustafa is a descendant of the jurist al-Shafiʻi
flags.note: The record gives no date of visit, office or country of origin, so the guest cannot be identified from the text. The occasion of the poem should be supplied by the Sheikh’s office before the record is displayed.

translator_notes: An occasional poem of welcome, not a fatwa. type is set to "article" for want of a verse type in the schema; it states no ruling and none has been inferred.
Rendered as prose line by line per style guide section 4; no rhymed English attempted.

الإمام الشافعي here is the guest’s father as a living titleholder, not Muhammad ibn Idris al-Shafiʻi the eponym of the school. The English keeps it as a name so that the record cannot be misread as concerning the jurist.
قبلة المظلوم is rendered "the qiblah of the wronged": the metaphor is of a direction all turn towards, and flattening it to "refuge" would lose the image the poet chose.

SOURCE DEFECT. The Arabic as served breaks a word mid-way at قبلة ال مظلوم (for المظلوم), the same two-column-scrape artefact that affects 1113 in this range. Preserved verbatim in body_ar, not reproduced in body_en, and to be cleaned corpus-wide rather than per record (style guide section 11).
